clinician.final_diagnosis: Central lymphatic congestion (CLC) and superior vena cava (SVC) syndrome
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 64-year-old woman with a 20-pack-year smoking history and persistent cough was diagnosed with stage IV lung adenocarcinoma with EGFR mutation and brain metastases. Two weeks after drug-induced interstitial pneumonia onset, she developed prominent neck and face edema, erythema, and dyspnea. Contrast-enhanced CT revealed severe SVC stenosis consistent with SVC syndrome. She also developed painless erythema and induration of the chest and abdomen. Skin biopsy of erythematic lesions showed neoplastic cells within dermal lymphatic vessels, confirming lymphatic tumor embolism consistent with central lymphatic congestion (CLC). Angiography and balloon dilation restored SVC blood flow but only temporarily improved cervicofacial edema and dyspnea. Subsequent chest CT showed persistent SVC constriction, implying other causes contributing to symptom persistence, consistent with combined CLC and SVC syndrome causing the patient's edema and dyspnea.
